description: The Snowpark Java classes an inline handler names: Row, Column, Functions, and the types trio StructType / StructField / DataTypes. The point of each test is that a handler written against the REAL Snowpark API COMPILES AND RUNS UNCHANGED - before these classes existed, collect() handed back frostlake's own storage row, whose only accessor is getValue(int), so rows[0].getString(0) did not compile at all. On a live run the very same handler SOURCE is compiled by Snowflake against the real Snowpark, so every line here is a TWO-SIDED claim: a method the stub offers but Snowpark does not will not compile there, and a value the stub prints differently will not match. That is what makes this the stub's SPECIFICATION rather than a description of it - which is why the assertions are on VALUES and on the vocabulary the real API prints, never on generated SQL text, which Snowpark builds its own way and never exposes. Two printed vocabularies matter: typeName() is the type's CLASS name (LongType, not Long) while toString() matches it except for DECIMAL, the one type carrying parameters, and a StructField prints its type in the SHORT vocabulary instead. A quoted field name keeps its case AND its quotes where an unquoted one is folded; negation is spelled unary_not() and not not(); and getName() answers a name for a plain column and nothing for a composed expression. Converted 1:1 from scripting/SnowparkApiSurfaceTest (now retired); its call() helper created a procedure per test and CALLed it, which is exactly what the steps here do.
